A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text, figures, equations and appendices A–E. The complete material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Appendix E and Figure 7 report original permutation-training experiments with 50,000-hidden-unit networks. Appendix B also reports numerical validation of algorithm execution.

after.justification: v4 retains these original training experiments and numerical validations, including Figure 7’s measured accuracy and ensemble-size results.

M1.justification: Sections 4–6 retain the same template matching, orthonormal encoding, two-layer ReLU networks, ensemble averaging and sign-based rounding. Appendix B’s algorithmic instructions are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both retain numerical checks for binary permutation, addition and multiplication, and finite-network training experiments on permutation in Appendix E. No evaluated dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Figures 5 and 7 retain the same comparisons against theoretical ensemble-complexity estimates and bounds. Neither version introduces or removes an evaluated competing learning method.

E3.justification: Appendix E retains 50,000 hidden units, full-batch gradient descent, standard-basis training inputs and 1,000 random test vectors with two nonzero entries. The input-length and ensemble-size experiments have the same settings.

E4.justification: The existing input-length and ensemble-size analyses in Figures 5 and 7 and the numerical correctness checks are retained. No ablation, robustness test or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both describe independently trained ensemble members and present the same curves without empirical uncertainty intervals. No seed specifications, repeated-trial counts or statistical testing practices are added or revised.

E6.justification: Figure 5’s numerical ensemble-complexity curves and Figure 7’s measured ensemble sizes for 90% accuracy and accuracy curves are unchanged. Appendix B’s reported numerical validation through 10-bit inputs is also retained.

T1.justification: Appendix D.1 inserts the missing equality before −2π(3π−1)k′/(2π−1)² in the calculation of u−2a, correcting an erroneous subtraction in the displayed identity. The surrounding proof strategy, assumptions, theorems and asymptotic conclusions are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and closing section retain the same claims of exact algorithmic execution with high probability using logarithmically many training examples, covering permutations, addition, multiplication and SBN instructions.

C2.justification: Section 7 retains the limitations concerning orthogonal data, explicit instruction access and bounded memory requiring retraining for larger inputs. Appendix E retains its computational-resource explanation for restricting finite-network experiments to permutation.

D1.justification: Appendix B changes the documented code location from opallab/binary_algos to watcl-lab/binary_algos on GitHub. v4 also adds the updated address to the main-text supplementary-material footnote; other implementation disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research-positioning arguments in Section 2 are unchanged. The reference list matches after accounting for pagination.

P1.justification: v4 fixes subject–verb agreement in Section 2, removes a duplicated 'the' in Section 3 and corrects 'Intruction count' in Appendix B. The overall narrative and section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 reorders the test-vector labels to match the training matrices and adjusts column-heading sizes. Appendix D’s equations are reflowed, and Figure 7’s existing discussion moves below the figure. The result plots remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 resolves the label mismatch in Figure 3 and repairs the displayed eigenvalue identity in Appendix D.1, improving internal consistency. Grammar fixes and updated code-access instructions provide additional modest benefits. The scientific scope, empirical evidence and limitations remain stable.
